units.sourceHTML: The sdiff command merges two files and interactively outputs the results. Its arguments are as follows:

units.text: This merges ⟦0⟧ with ⟦1⟧, with output to ⟦2⟧. If ⟦3⟧ is a directory and ⟦4⟧ is not, ⟦5⟧ compares the file in ⟦6⟧ whose file name is that of ⟦7⟧, and vice versa. ⟦8⟧ and ⟦9⟧ may not both be directories.
units.sourceHTML: This merges from-file with to-file, with output to outfile. If from-file is a directory and to-file is not, sdiff compares the file in from-file whose file name is that of to-file, and vice versa. from-file and to-file may not both be directories.

units.text: ⟦0⟧ options begin with ‘⟦1⟧’, so normally ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ may not begin with ‘⟦4⟧’. However, ⟦5⟧ as an argument by itself treats the remaining arguments as file names even if they begin with ‘⟦6⟧’. You may not use ⟦7⟧ as an input file.
units.sourceHTML: sdiff options begin with ‘-’, so normally from-file and to-file may not begin with ‘-’. However, -- as an argument by itself treats the remaining arguments as file names even if they begin with ‘-’. You may not use - as an input file.

units.text: ⟦0⟧ without ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧) produces a side-by-side difference. This usage is obsolete; use the ⟦3⟧ (⟦4⟧) option of ⟦5⟧ instead.
units.sourceHTML: sdiff without --output (-o) produces a side-by-side difference. This usage is obsolete; use the --side-by-side (-y) option of diff instead.

units.text: An exit status of 0 means no differences were found, 1 means some differences were found, and 2 means trouble.
units.sourceHTML: An exit status of 0 means no differences were found, 1 means some differences were found, and 2 means trouble.
